text:
Maya: Hey team, customer ACME Corp hit an error on the embeddings endpoint when sending batched inputs. They see a \"dimension mismatch\" error. Posting logs and minimal repro below. Customer is blocked for search relevance tests. :frowning:

Raj: FYI this started after we rolled a small client-side change to batch multiple docs into one request. Error from our gateway: \"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 768\"\n\nMaya: Customer code snippet (Python):
```python
resp = client.embeddings.create(
  model='text-embed-1536',
  input=["doc1", "doc2", "doc3"]
)
# they say resp['data'] contains vectors of length 768 for some items
```

Maya: Raw gateway trace id: trace-7a2c (attached). They used batch_size=3 and also tried batch_size=1 which returned consistent 1536 dims. So it looks batch path is returning wrong sized vectors intermittently.

Liam: @Maya can you confirm model name exactly from their request headers? If they accidentally hit a different model alias we sometimes fallback to a legacy smaller-dim model for compatibility. Also need the input payload shape they POSTed (json).

Maya: Pasting their request body (redacted):
```json
{"model":"text-embed-1536","input":["A","B","C"],"batching":{"enabled":true,"max_batch_size":8}}
```

Olivia: I've pulled the node logs for trace-7a2c. The router forwarded the request to host pool gpu-02 which runs the v2 runtime. I see two back-to-back requests from the same trace being coalesced by the batching layer, then routed to a different runtime instance that advertises a different model_variant id: \"text-embed-768-compat\". Looks like smart-routing fallback kicked in because gpu-02 reported transient memory pressure.

Liam: That explains the dims. Workaround: ensure requests pin model_variant (or set routing policy to strict) so fallback doesn't substitute smaller models. For hosted API the client can set `preferred_variants: ["text-embed-1536"]` in the request. We'll document the header too.

eng-ml-oncall: Quick mitigation for customer: ask them to set batching.enabled=false or reduce `max_batch_size` to 1 while we fix routing behavior. Also adding a server-side guard so mixed-dimension batch responses are rejected instead of returned.

Raj: Customer tested with batching.enabled=false and confirmed all vectors now length 1536. They still need batching for throughput; their throughput target is ~1200 reqs/min.

Liam: For throughput with correct dims, recommended options: 1) pin variant as above, 2) set `preferred_variants` and `timeout_ms` slightly higher to avoid fallback, 3) use our dedicated capacity (Reserved/Dedicated) if they need consistent placement. Also note that when the router falls back we currently don't rewrite the error to be more actionable — that's a docs gap.

Maya: I'm drafting an email to the customer with the immediate workaround (disable batching / pin variant) and ETA for a server fix. Can someone own the runbook/update?

product-docs: Assigning to product-docs to add an FAQ entry and a short runbook: 
- Why dimension mismatch happens with batching (router fallbacks & mixed model variants)
- Customer workarounds (disable batching, pin variant, use Dedicated)
- Example request snippets to pin variants and recommended batch sizes for common models

product-docs: Proposed doc snippet for API: 
```json
{
  "model": "text-embed-1536",
  "input": ["..."],
  "preferred_variants": ["text-embed-1536"],
  "batching": {"enabled": true, "max_batch_size": 16}
}
```

Olivia: Operational follow-up: I'll add a hotfix to the router so that when coalesced requests would be routed to an incompatible variant we either 1) fail the request with clear error \"incompatible model variant for batched request\" or 2) split the batch and route separately. Prefer option 1 for now to avoid silent wrong-dimension responses.

Liam: After router patch we should run a quick canary: simulate coalesced requests under memory pressure and verify we return a deterministic error instead of mixed-dim outputs.

Maya: Thanks all — I'll send customer the workaround update now and mark this as escalated. Leaving follow-ups: Olivia implements router guard (ETA 4h), product-docs adds FAQ (ETA EOD), eng-ml to check whether we can make variant pinning honored by default for embeddings (triage).

Raj: Customer replied: appreciated, will accept temporary disable of batching. Please keep me in loop. :thumbsup:

Maya: Closing the support ticket once Olivia confirms hotfix deployed. Will post final closure message here. :white_check_mark:
